The National Institute of Social Defence was set up originally as the Central Bureau of Correctional Services in 1961, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, in pursuance of the recommendations emerging at various National Forums. In 1964, the Bureau was transferred to the then Department of Social Security.

Since 1975, the Institute was a subordinate office under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The National Institute of Social Defence has become an Autonomous Body vide Government of India Notification No. 10-3/2000-SD. Vol. II, dated July 15, 2002, and is registered under the Societies Act XXI of 1860 with the Government of NCT, Delhi.

The National Institute of Social Defence is the nodal training and research institute in the field of social defence. Though social defence covers the entire gamut of activities and programmes for the protection of society, it is currently focusing on human resource development in the areas of drug abuse prevention, welfare of senior citizens and transgenders, beggary prevention, and other social defence issues.

What is the National Institute of Social Defence?
• NISD is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.
• NISD is a centre to carry out research on social defence.
• NISD coordinates and liaises between the government and the non-government organisations at state, national and international levels.
• The institute develops preventive, curative and rehabilitative tools, programmes and policies in the field of social defence, and also undertakes research, training, consultancy, documentation and publication in the field.

Mandate
The mandate of the institute is to provide inputs for the social defence programmes of the Government of India through training, research and documentation.

sections.heading: Vision & Mission
sections.html:
Vision
Fostering public sensitivity towards issues related to marginalised sections of society, including old age persons and victims of substance abuse, and strengthening effective service delivery.

Mission
Enhancing the capacities of service providers. Working towards a wider dissemination of information in the field of old age care, victims of substance abuse, and other social defence issues through training, research and documentation.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.html:
The main objectives of the institute are to:
• Review the policies and programmes in the field of social defence
• Anticipate and diagnose the problems in the field of social defence
• Develop preventive, curative and rehabilitative policies in the field
• Identify and develop the instruments for realizing the objectives of social defence policies
• Review and evaluate the implementation of social defence policies and programmes
• Develop and promote voluntary efforts in social defence

In order to realize the above objectives, the institute carries out the following:
• Research on social defence issues.
• Compilation and analysis of statistics in the areas of social defence
• Develop, promote, sponsor and undertake training/orientation in the field of social defence
• Advice the Central and State Governments / Union Territory Administrations on social defence problems and provide technical inputs for preparation of model rules and regulations in the field of social defence
• Provide a forum for exchange of information on social defence among the State / Union Territories and voluntary organizations, and serve as a clearing house for information in the field
• Create public awareness on social defence problems especially regarding preventive and rehabilitative roles of the community
• Assist the Government of India for exchange of information on social defence with other countries and with the United Nations for their specialized agencies
• Organise conferences / seminars/ workshops on social defence
• Establish liaison with universities, research institutes and voluntary organizations in the area of social defence
• Bring out publications in the field of social defence, both popular and professional.

Areas of concern
• Substance Abuse Prevention
• Care of Older Persons, and
• Other Social Defence issues including Beggary Prevention, and welfare of Transgenders.

Target groups
The target group of the institute are:
• Functionaries of concerned departments of the Central and State Governments
• Service providers/ caregivers working in the area of social defence both in the voluntary sector and the Government.
• Academicians and professionals of schools of social work and concerned academic institutions.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.html:
With the rapid increase in the ageing population and the changing structure of families and communities, the demand for organised, accessible and quality care services for senior citizens has increased significantly. Senior Citizens often require varying levels of assistance related to health, mobility, nutrition, personal care, emotional well-being, social participation and management of age-related conditions.

Recognising these emerging needs, the Senior Citizens Division of NISD has been actively engaged for over a decade in strengthening the elderly-care sector through capacity building, training, awareness generation, development of skilled human resources and promotion of professional standards in geriatric care.

One of the major initiatives of the Division is the development and implementation of the Geriatric Care Provider (GCP) Qualification/Job Role – QP Code: GCP/HSS/Q0101, which is designed to create a pool of professionally trained caregivers capable of providing safe, dignified, compassionate and person-centred care to senior citizens.

sections.heading: 2. Senior Citizens Division of NISD
sections.html:
The Senior Citizens Division is one of the key programme divisions of NISD and focuses on strengthening the national response to issues concerning ageing and the welfare of older persons.

The Division works towards enhancing the quality of care and support available to senior citizens through systematic capacity building of professionals, caregivers, service providers, institutions and other stakeholders working in the field of ageing.

Its interventions are guided by the principles of:

  • dignity and respect for Senior Citizens;
  • healthy and active ageing;
  • independence and autonomy;
  • safety and protection;
  • person-centred care;
  • social inclusion and participation;
  • professionalization of elderly-care services; and
  • Development of a sustainable care ecosystem and
  • Research activities.

sections.heading: 3. Major Areas of Work of the Senior Citizens Division
sections.html: The Senior Citizens Division undertakes a range of activities aimed at strengthening Senior Citizen care services and enhancing institutional and human-resource capacities.

sections.heading: 3.1 Capacity Building and Training
sections.html:
The Division organises capacity-building programmes like Dementia Care & Management, Geriatric Counselling, basic geriatric care, outreach Programme for the family members on Primary Care for different categories of stakeholders involved in the care and welfare of senior citizens. These include caregivers, trainers, assessors, social workers, nursing professionals, healthcare personnel, and functionaries of senior citizen homes, civil society organisations and other professionals working in the ageing sector.

The training programmes focus on both theoretical understanding and practical competencies required for working effectively with Senior Citizens.

sections.heading: 3.2 Skill Development in Geriatric Care
sections.html:
An important area of intervention is the development of a skilled workforce for senior citizens care. The Division promotes structured and competency-based training to ensure that caregivers possess the knowledge, practical abilities, values and attitudes required to provide quality care.

The Geriatric Care Provider Qualification represents a major step towards standardising caregiving competencies and professionalising the elderly-care workforce.

sections.heading: 3.3 Training of Master Trainers and Assessors
sections.html:
To ensure quality and uniformity in training and assessment, NISD conducts Training of Trainers (ToT) and Training of Assessors (ToA) programmes.

The Training of Trainers programmes aim to develop qualified Master Trainers who can deliver the prescribed curriculum effectively, while Training of Assessors programmes create a pool of competent assessors capable of conducting fair, transparent and competency-based assessments in accordance with prescribed standards.

sections.heading: 3.4 Awareness and Sensitisation
sections.html: The Division also promotes awareness regarding the Inter-generation bonding, holistic health, geriatric diet & nutrition, therapies, Maintenance and welfare of parents and Senior Citizens Act (MWPSC Act), rights, needs and concerns of senior citizens. Sensitisation programmes help stakeholders understand ageing from a holistic perspective and encourage greater respect, empathy and social responsibility towards senior citizens.

sections.heading: 3.5 Development of Training Resources
sections.html:
NISD develops and updates training materials, guidelines, course content, assessment tools and other resource materials relating to geriatric care and the welfare of senior citizens.

These resources facilitate standardised implementation of training programmes across different institutions and geographical locations.

sections.heading: 3.6 Promotion of Healthy and Active Ageing
sections.html:
The Division promotes approaches that enable senior citizens to remain physically active, mentally healthy, socially connected and independent for as long as possible.

Training and awareness programmes therefore emphasise preventive healthcare, nutrition, exercise, yoga, meditation, emotional well-being, social engagement and age-friendly practices.

sections.heading: 4.1. Need for Professional Geriatric Care
sections.html:
This program aims to develop Geriatric Care Providers dedicated to providing high quality care and support to senior citizens. It offers comprehensive, evidence-based training in geriatric care, equipping caregivers with sub-nursing skills, taking care of an older person who has a chronic illness or disease, elderly in doing their activities of daily living and to fulfill local requirements like shopping, going for physiotherapy, Helping in medications or talking to doctors and nurses on behalf of client/patient, Helping to bathe or dress someone who is frail or disabled; or taking care of household work, meals, or bills for someone who cannot do these things alone (Including taking the elderly to the park/bank on wheel chair) and a deep understanding of the critical role empathy plays in caregiving. Additionally, the course emphasizes the importance of self-care to ensure the well-being of caregivers themselves. With a strong focus on practical skills, the training prepares caregivers to deliver effective interventions in family and community settings, promoting the welfare and quality of life of older adults. Building Geriatric Caregivers as Digital Health Assistance

India is witnessing significant demographic changes, including a steady increase in the number and proportion of senior citizens. Increased longevity is a positive development; however, it also creates new requirements in healthcare, long-term care, home-based assistance, rehabilitation, dementia care and social support.

Several older persons may experience:

  • reduced mobility and functional ability;
  • chronic or multiple health conditions;
  • sensory impairment;
  • cognitive decline or dementia;
  • nutritional concerns;
  • social isolation and loneliness;
  • dependence in activities of daily living;
  • risk of falls and injuries;
  • emotional or psychological concerns; and
  • Increased need for home-based or institutional care.

At the same time, traditional family-based caregiving arrangements are undergoing changes due to urbanisation, migration, smaller families and changing employment patterns.

These factors underline the need for an organised and professionally trained caregiving workforce.

A trained Geriatric Care Provider can play a crucial role in bridging the gap between older persons, families and professional healthcare systems by providing day-to-day assistance, monitoring, companionship and appropriate supportive care.

sections.heading: 4.2. Geriatric Care Provider Qualification/Job Role
sections.html:
The Geriatric Care Provider (GCP) Qualification/Job Role, bearing QP Code: GCP/HSS/Q0101, has been developed by the National Institute of Social Defence to address the increasing demand for trained elderly-care personnel.

The Qualification has been approved by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) and is aligned with the national vocational education and skill-development framework.

The qualification provides a structured pathway for developing individuals into competent geriatric caregivers through a combination of classroom instruction, demonstrations, practical exercises and workplace exposure.

sections.heading: 4.3. Aim of the Geriatric Care Provider Course
sections.html:
The primary aim of the programme is to create a trained, qualified, competent and compassionate workforce capable of providing safe, dignified and person-centred care to senior citizens.

The programme seeks to strengthen both the technical competencies and interpersonal qualities of caregivers so that senior citizens receive care that respects their individual needs, preferences, privacy and dignity.

sections.heading: 4.4. Objectives of the Training Programme
sections.html:
The major objectives of the Geriatric Care Provider course are to:

1. develop a skilled workforce capable of supporting senior citizens in different care settings;
2. provide trainees with a comprehensive understanding of ageing and age-related changes;
3. build competencies in assisting older persons with activities of daily living;
4. strengthen knowledge regarding basic health monitoring and geriatric health concerns;
5. promote safe and hygienic caregiving practices;
6. enhance communication, empathy, companionship and interpersonal skills;
7. develop competencies in nutrition and feeding support for senior citizens;
8. strengthen knowledge relating to dementia and cognitive impairment;
9. develop skills in mobility assistance, fall prevention and use of assistive devices;
10. provide basic knowledge and practical competency in first aid and emergency response;
11. promote infection prevention and control practices;
12. develop understanding of caregiver ethics, confidentiality, boundaries and professional conduct;
13. promote healthy, active and productive ageing;
14. emphasise caregiver self-care and prevention of burnout; and
15. Improve the overall quality, safety and accessibility of geriatric-care services.

sections.heading: 4.5. Duration and Level of the Course
sections.html:
The Geriatric Care Provider Training Course has a total duration of 480 hours, including 138 hours of On-the-Job Training (OJT)/internship.

The qualification is aligned with NSQF Level 4.

The programme integrates:

• theoretical learning;
• practical demonstrations;
• hands-on skill training;
• role plays and case-based learning;
• simulation exercises;
• supervised practice;
• assignments and internal evaluation
• Orientation visits and
• Field-based On-the-Job Training.

This integrated approach enables trainees to apply classroom knowledge in real-life care situations.

sections.heading: 4.6. Course Covered under the modules
sections.html:
The course provides comprehensive exposure to the various dimensions of geriatric care.

1) Introduction to Geriatric / Elderly Care/ Government policies and programs
2) Body System, functions & related problems in Elderly
3) Mental Health Issues in Elderly
4) Communication, Empathy & Companionship
5) Infection Prevention & Control
6) Nutrition
7) Positions, Comfort Devices & Assistive Devices
8) Caring Procedures & Therapies
9) Self-Care of Geriatric Caregivers
10) Financial Literacy and
11) Digital Health Assistance

sections.heading: 4.7. Training Methodology
sections.html:
The Geriatric Care Provider programme adopts a competency-based and participatory training methodology.

Training is delivered through a combination of:

• classroom lectures;
• interactive discussions;
• audio-visual presentations;
• demonstrations;
• practical sessions;
• simulation exercises;
• case studies;
• role plays;
• group exercises;
• assignments; and
• supervised practice

The focus is not merely on acquiring theoretical knowledge but on demonstrating practical competency in real caregiving situations.

On-the-Job Training / Internship

A significant component of the course is the 138 hours of On-the-Job Training (OJT)/internship.

OJT provides trainees with an opportunity to apply their acquired knowledge and skills under supervised conditions.

Depending on approved arrangements, exposure may be provided in suitable settings such as; hospitals, geriatric-care institutions;

The OJT component enables trainees to understand real-world caregiving challenges and strengthens their confidence, professional behaviour and practical competence.

sections.heading: 4.8. Assessment and Certification
sections.html:
Assessment is an important component of competency-based training.

Trainees are expected to demonstrate prescribed knowledge and practical skills in accordance with the assessment criteria of the qualification.

Assessment may include:

• theory-based evaluation;
• oral questioning;
• practical demonstration;
• observation of skills;
• case-based evaluation; and
• Assessment of required occupational competencies.

The assessment process is intended to ensure that successful candidates possess the minimum competencies necessary for safe and effective geriatric care.

Candidates successfully completing the prescribed training and assessment requirements become eligible for certification in accordance with the applicable qualification and certification framework.

sections.heading: 4.9. Contribution to Healthy, Active and Dignified Ageing
sections.html:
The ultimate objective of elderly-care services should not be limited to providing assistance when an older person becomes dependent.

Care systems should also promote:

• health;
• independence;
• functionality;
• social participation;
• emotional well-being;
• autonomy;
• security; and
• Dignity.

A professionally trained caregiver can help an older person continue to live as independently and meaningfully as possible.

The GCP programme therefore contributes not only to caregiving but also to the larger national objective of promoting healthy, active, safe and dignified ageing.

sections.heading: 4.10. Potential Areas of Engagement
sections.html:
After successful training and certification, Geriatric Care Providers may find opportunities in a variety of elderly-care environments, including:

• home-based elderly care;
• senior citizen homes;
• assisted-living facilities;
• hospitals;
• rehabilitation centres;
• community-based elderly-care programmes;
• day-care centres for senior citizens;
• palliative and supportive-care settings, subject to role requirements;
• non-governmental organisations working with older persons; and
• Professional caregiving service agencies.

The qualification can therefore support both employment and self-employment opportunities in the growing care sector.

sections.heading: 4.11. Contribution to the Care Economy
sections.html:
The Geriatric Care Provider programme has wider significance in the context of India’s emerging care economy.

A well-functioning care economy requires:

• trained human resources;
• standardised qualifications;
• quality training institutions;
• credible assessment and certification;
• appropriate care infrastructure;
• career pathways for caregivers;
• public awareness; and
• Coordination between families, communities, government agencies, healthcare institutions and service providers.

By developing a formal qualification and establishing systems for training, assessment and certification, NISD is contributing towards the professionalization of elderly care.

The programme can also support employment generation, particularly in a sector where the demand for trained personnel is expected to continue increasing with demographic ageing.

sections.heading: 5. Training of Trainers
sections.html:
Quality training requires competent trainers who possess both subject knowledge and effective teaching skills.

Accordingly, NISD conducts Training of Trainers (ToT) programmes for the Geriatric Care Provider Job Role.

The ToT programme aims to:

• familiarise trainers with the Qualification Pack and curriculum;
• strengthen knowledge of geriatric-care competencies;
• improve teaching and facilitation skills;
• promote competency-based training methodology;
• standardise practical demonstrations;
• strengthen adult-learning approaches; and
• Ensure uniform delivery of the course.

A trained pool of Master Trainers contributes significantly to maintaining national-level quality standards in geriatric-care training.

sections.heading: 6. Training of Assessors
sections.html:
NISD also conducts Training of Assessors (ToA) programmes to develop a qualified pool of assessors for the Geriatric Care Provider qualification.

Assessors are trained in:

• understanding the Qualification Pack;
• assessment criteria;
• competency-based assessment;
• theory and practical evaluation;
• evidence collection;
• observation techniques;
• documentation;
• objectivity and impartiality;
• professional ethics; and
• Maintenance of quality standards.

The ToA programme supports fair, reliable and transparent assessment and certification processes.

NCDAP

What is the 3-Month Certificate Course on Drug De-Addiction, Counseling Skills, and Rehabilitation offered by NISD?

The 3-Month Certificate Course is a comprehensive training program conducted by the NCDAP division of NISD. It is designed to equip participants with practical knowledge and skills in drug de-addiction, psychosocial counseling, and rehabilitation of individuals affected by substance use disorders. The course includes theoretical sessions, case studies, field visits, and hands-on experience to prepare professionals, social workers, and NGO staff for effective fieldwork in the area of drug abuse prevention and treatment.

Who can apply for the 3-Month Certificate Course, and what are the eligibility criteria?

The course is open to individuals with a background in social work, psychology, sociology, public health, or any related field. Preference is given to professionals working in NGOs, rehabilitation centers, or government organizations dealing with substance use issues. Fresh graduates interested in building a career in addiction counseling and rehabilitation may also apply. Applicants are expected to have a strong commitment to community service and a passion for working in the social defence sector.

What is the objective of the One-Day Awareness Generation Program, and who can participate?

The One-Day Awareness Generation Program aims to educate and sensitize various community stakeholders—including students, teachers, parents, community leaders, and youth volunteers—about the ill effects of drug abuse and the importance of early prevention. These programs are interactive and often include expert talks, group discussions, film screenings, and informational materials. Participation is open to all and is especially encouraged for educational institutions and grassroots organizations.

Is there any certification provided upon completion of these training programs?

Yes, participants who successfully complete the 3-Month Certificate Course receive an official Certificate from NISD, endorsed by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India. For the One-Day Awareness Generation Programs, participants are also awarded a participation certificate recognizing their involvement and contribution to spreading awareness on drug abuse prevention.

How can I enroll or get more information about NCDAP-NISD’s training programs?

You can visit the official website of NISD at www.nisd.gov.in for the latest updates, application forms, course schedules, and contact information. You may also reach out directly to the NCDAP Division via email or phone as listed on the website. Periodic announcements are made regarding upcoming training batches and awareness events, so keeping an eye on the updates section is highly recommended.

Senior Citizens

What are the activities the Senior Citizen Division of NISD does?

The Senior Citizen Division of NISD undertakes a variety of activities, which include:

I. Awareness/Sensitization Programmes
II. Capacity Development Programmes including TOT: Geriatric Care Providers Training Course (NCVET approved), One Month Advanced Courses, One Year PG Diploma Courses.
III. Conference/Workshops / Seminars/Consultations
IV. Outreach Programmes like Health Camps, Digital Literacy etc.,
V. Research Activities on Elderly Issues
VI. Special Events – Observation & Celebration of International Days

List of places where training programmes are conducted?

Training programmes are implemented nationwide through Regional Resource Training Centres (RRTCs) and Other Collaborating Agencies (OCAs).

Are the training programmes free of cost?

Yes, all training programmes under NISD are offered free of cost.

Who are the beneficiaries of the training programmes conducted by NISD?

The beneficiaries of the training programmes conducted by NISD are the following:

i. Senior Citizens (Majorly)
ii. Family Member of Senior Citizens
iii. Grant In Aid Institutions supported by the Ministry/ State Government
iv. Healthcare Workers
v. Police Personnels
vi. NGO Functionaries
vii. Academicians
viii. Research Scholars
ix. Policy Makers
x. University/College Students
xi. School Students

Are there any training programmes for Family Members of Senior Citizen?

Yes, there is a training programme for Family Members of Senior Citizen called as Five (5) Days outreach Programme for the family members on Primary Care.

Are there any training programme on Dementia Care & Management?

Yes, there is a training programme on Dementia Care & Management called as “Three days Residential Training Programme on Dementia Care and Management.”

How can the Citizens attend the training programmes funded by NISD?

Interested individuals can visit NISD website for getting an updated training calendar regarding the venue & date of the programme.

What kinds of programmes are undertaken by NISD?

The following kinds of programmes are undertaken by NISD:

I. Awareness/Sensitisation programme
II. Residential/Non-residential Training Programme
III. Conference/Workshops / Seminars/Consultations
IV. Outreach Programmes
V. Special Events

What all topics are covered in Awareness/Sensitisation programmes?

The topics which are covered in Awareness/Sensitisation training programmes are as follows:

I. MWPSC Act, 2007
II. Inter-generational Bonding in Colleges & Schools
III. Digitalisation & Cyber Security
IV. Holistic Heath including Yoga, Natural Therapy & Physiotherapy
V. Diet and Nutrition
VI. Awareness Programme on Common Physical & Mental Health Issues among elderly

What all topics are covered in Residential/Non-residential Training Programme?

The topics which are covered in Residential/Non-residential Training Programmes are as follows:

I. Three days Residential Training Programme on Basic Geriatric Care
II. Three days Residential Training Programme on Geriatric Counseling
III. Three days Residential Training Programme on Dementia Care and Management
IV. Three days Residential Training Programme on Yoga for Senior Citizens, Physiotherapy, Naturopathy etc.
V. 3 days Training Programme on Music Therapy and other related therapies.
VI. 3 days Training Programme on Common Health Problems/issues and Importance of immunization schedule among Sr. Citizens (Residential/Non-residential)

What all topics are covered in Conference / Workshops / Seminars / Consultations?

The topics which are covered in Residential/Non-residential Training Programmes are as follows:

I. Two Days National Level Conference / Workshops / Seminars on Elderly Issues
II. Two Days State Level Conference / Workshops / Seminars on Elderly Issues

What all topics are covered in Outreach Programmes?

The topics which are covered in Outreach Programmes Programmes are as follows:

I. Health Camp
II. Digital Literacy
III. Meditation/Spiritual Camps
IV. Five (5) Days outreach Programme for the family members on Primary Care
V. One Day Inter-generation Mela /Traditional Fashion Shows

What all Special Events are Observed & Celebrated in NISD?

The following Special Events are Observed & Celebrated in NISD:

I. World Elder Abuse Awareness Day
II. International Day of Yoga
III. World Alzheimer’s Day
IV. International Day of Older Persons

Are the programmes online or offline?

The Programmes are majorly offline but few programmes are conducted online as well.

Are there online training programmes? What are they?

Yes, online training programmes are conducted by NISD. The online training programme is on Elderly Issues

What are the different long term courses under Senior Citizen Division of NISD?

There are two types of long term Course of Senior Citizen Division of NISD:

I. One Month advance Course on Palliative & Hospice Care.

II. One Month advance Course on Dementia Care.

III. Three-month Certificate Course in Geriatric Care for Bedside Assistance.

IV. One-year Postgraduate Diploma in Integrated Geriatric Care (PGDIGC).

When was the first one year PG Diploma in Integrated Geriatric Care launched?

The first one year PG Diploma in Integrated Geriatric Care launched on 1st October 2003.

What is the class timing and the requirement of attendance for completing the course?

The class timing is 10.00 AM to 4.00 PM. Minimum 80% of attendance is required for giving final examination.

What is the eligibility for one –year PGDIGC?

Graduation from a recognized University.

What is the total Hrs and Credit Points of the Course?

The total Hrs of the course is 950 Hrs and it has 42 credit point.

What is the course curriculum of one year PGDIGC?

The course curriculum includes Multidisciplinary Perspectives on Social Gerontology, Health & Ageing, Planning for Services In Geriatric Care, Management of Care-Giving In Public Institutions and Home Care, Introduction to Gerontological Research Methodology Policies and Programmes for Care of Elderly and Senior Citizens and Role of Gerontological Social Work Practitioner.

What are the main academic inputs under one-year PGDIGC?

(i) Class Presentation

(ii) Orientation visit to Age Care Institutions

(iii) Group Report

(iv) Concurrent Field Visit

(v) Placement

What are the career opportunities for one-year PGDIGC?

The students on successful completion of these courses can find jobs in the Govt. or Non-Govt. Institutions working for old age care as:

  • Project Director and Programme Managers
  • Social Protection Officer in Helapge India
  • HRD Professionals
  • Counselors and Consultants in Community Based Organizations
  • Associates with Residents Welfare Association (RWA)
  • Welfare Officers / Middle level Professional in Hospitals/Nursing Homes.
What is the eligibility of Three- month course?

(a) Minimum qualification of 10th pass. Exception to be made to an extent of 10 % (2 students in a batch of 25) for deserving candidates who have educational qualification of 8th pass.

(b) Minimum age limit with 18 years (in completed years).

(c) Should have a valid Aadhar card.

(d) Should not be indulged in any substance abuse.

(e) Should have documentary proof of age and residence.

(f) Police verification (optional)

(g) Should have a valid education proof.

What is the course curriculum of Three Month Course in Geriatric care?

i. Geriatric/Elderly Care- Introduction

ii. Body system, functions and related problems in Elderly

iii. Mental health issues/concerns in Elderly

iv. Communication, Empathy & Companionship

v. Infection and control

vi. Nutrition

vii. Positions, comfort devices and assistive devices

viii. Caring procedures

What are the main academic inputs under Three Month Course in Geriatric care?

Orientation visits to Senior Citizen Homes, Around 40 nursing practical demonstrations, One Month Internship in Hospital, submission of log book, Placement through campus interview

What are the career opportunities for six-month course?

Career opportunities may be available in the form of:

  • Home Care
  • Social worker
  • Emergency relief worker
  • Health worker
  • Project assistant
  • Physiotherapy Assistant
  • Assistant- Mobile- Medicare unit.
  • Nursing Assistant
  • Home Nursing Assistant

Elderline

When was the Elderline-National Helpline for Senior Citisens (NHSC) Scheme/Project launched?

The Elderline-National Helpline for Senior Citizens (NHSC) was officially launched by Former Vice-President Sh.M.Venkaiah Naidu on October 1, 2021 during observation of the International Day of Older Persons at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.

Who are the coordinating agencies of the Elderline Scheme/Project?

The project is an initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE), Government of India. It is operated in collaboration with National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), a training and research institute under MoSJE, and State Government Departments/Implementing Agencies.

What is the short code Toll-Free number for the Elderline Scheme/Project?

The dedicated toll-free short code number for Elderline is 14567. It is accessible from both landline and mobile phones.

Who can avail the services provided by Elderline Scheme/Project?

Any senior citizen aged 60 years and above across India can avail the services. In emergency or rescue situations, family members or citizens may also reach out on their behalf.

What services does Elderline provide?

Elderline offers a wide range of services, including:

  • Information,
  • Guidance,
  • Counselling/Emotional Support and
  • Field Intervention
Are the services provided free of cost?

Yes, all services provided through Elderline are completely free of cost for senior citizens.

In how many States/UTs is the Elderline Scheme/Project operational?

As of now, the Elderline service is operational in 33 States and Union Territories of India, except Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal & Lakshadweep.

What is the time schedule during which the Elderline Scheme/Project call centers work?

The Elderline call centers operate daily from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, including weekends and public holidays, to ensure continuous support for senior citizens.

What should I do if I witness abuse or neglect of a senior citizen?

You can immediately call 14567 to report the incident. The call center will coordinate with local authorities and support agencies to provide the required assistance to the senior citizen concerned.

Are Elderline Services available in regional languages?

Yes, Elderline services are available in multiple regional languages to ensure accessibility for all senior citizens across different States.

What happens after a call is made to Elderline?

Once a call is received, a trained counselor listens and logs the issue. Depending on the nature of the problem, a field response team or appropriate service provider is engaged to take further action.

Can Elderline assist with senior citizen schemes and pensions?

Yes, Elderline provides information and guidance on various Central and State Government Schemes/Programmes, including those related to pensions, healthcare, and welfare programs for senior citizens.

एल्डरलाइन - राष्ट्रीय हेल्पलाइन योजना/परियोजना की शुरुआत कब हुई थी?

एल्डरलाइन – राष्ट्रीय हेल्पलाइन योजना/परियोजना का औपचारिक शुभारंभ पूर्व उपराष्ट्रपति श्री एम. वेंकैया नायडू द्वारा 1 अक्टूबर 2021 को “अंतरराष्ट्रीय वरिष्ठ नागरिक दिवस” के अवसर पर विज्ञान भवन, नई दिल्ली में किया गया था।

एल्डरलाइन योजना/परियोजना की समन्वय एजेंसियां कौन-कौन सी हैं?

यह परियोजना भारत सरकार के सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय (MoSJE) की एक पहल है। इसे मंत्रालय के तहत एक प्रशिक्षण एवं अनुसंधान संस्थान राष्ट्रीय सामाजिक रक्षा संस्थान (NISD) और राज्य सरकारों/क्रियान्वयन एजेंसियों के सहयोग से संचालित किया जाता है।

एल्डरलाइन योजना/परियोजना का शॉर्ट कोड टोल-फ्री नंबर क्या है?

एल्डरलाइन के लिए समर्पित शॉर्ट कोड टोल-फ्री नंबर 14567 है। यह लैंडलाइन और मोबाइल दोनों से उपलब्ध है।

एल्डरलाइन योजना/परियोजना की सेवाएं कौन प्राप्त कर सकता है?

भारत के किसी भी हिस्से में रहने वाले 60 वर्ष या उससे अधिक आयु के वरिष्ठ नागरिक इन सेवाओं का लाभ उठा सकते हैं। आपातकालीन या रेस्क्यू स्थितियों में, उनके परिवारजन या अन्य नागरिक भी उनकी ओर से संपर्क कर सकते हैं।

एल्डरलाइन कौन-कौन सी सेवाएं प्रदान करता है?

एल्डरलाइन निम्नलिखित सेवाएं प्रदान करता है:

  • जानकारी
  • मार्गदर्शन
  • परामर्श/भावनात्मक सहयोग
  • क्षेत्रीय हस्तक्षेप (फील्ड इंटरवेंशन)
क्या ये सेवाएं निःशुल्क हैं?

हाँ, एल्डरलाइन के माध्यम से प्रदान की जाने वाली सभी सेवाएं वरिष्ठ नागरिकों के लिए पूर्णतः निःशुल्क हैं।

एल्डरलाइन योजना/परियोजना कितने राज्यों/केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में चालू है?

वर्तमान में एल्डरलाइन सेवा भारत के 33 राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में कार्यरत है, आंध्र प्रदेश, पश्चिम बंगाल और लक्षद्वीप को छोड़कर।

एल्डरलाइन कॉल सेंटर किस समय अवधि में कार्य करता है?

एल्डरलाइन कॉल सेंटर प्रतिदिन सुबह 8:00 बजे से रात 8:00 बजे तक, सप्ताहांत और सार्वजनिक अवकाशों सहित कार्य करता है, ताकि वरिष्ठ नागरिकों को लगातार सहायता मिलती रहे।

यदि मैं किसी वरिष्ठ नागरिक के साथ दुर्व्यवहार या उपेक्षा देखूं तो क्या करूं?

आप तुरंत 14567 पर कॉल कर घटना की सूचना दे सकते हैं। कॉल सेंटर स्थानीय अधिकारियों और समर्थन एजेंसियों के साथ समन्वय कर संबंधित वरिष्ठ नागरिक को आवश्यक सहायता प्रदान करता है।

क्या एल्डरलाइन सेवाएं क्षेत्रीय भाषाओं में भी उपलब्ध हैं?

हाँ, एल्डरलाइन सेवाएं कई क्षेत्रीय भाषाओं में उपलब्ध हैं, ताकि सभी राज्यों के वरिष्ठ नागरिक आसानी से इसका उपयोग कर सकें।

एल्डरलाइन पर कॉल करने के बाद क्या होता है?

कॉल प्राप्त होते ही प्रशिक्षित परामर्शदाता आपकी बात सुनते हैं और समस्या को लॉग करते हैं। समस्या की प्रकृति के अनुसार, फील्ड प्रतिक्रिया टीम या उपयुक्त सेवा प्रदाता को कार्रवाई के लिए भेजा जाता है।

क्या एल्डरलाइन वरिष्ठ नागरिकों की योजनाओं और पेंशन में सहायता करता है?

हाँ, एल्डरलाइन केंद्र और राज्य सरकार की विभिन्न योजनाओं/कार्यक्रमों की जानकारी और मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करता है, जिनमें पेंशन, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल और वरिष्ठ नागरिकों के लिए कल्याणकारी कार्यक्रम शामिल हैं।

Transgender & Beggary

What is the name of Transgender Persons Act?

The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

When did The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act come intoforce?

On 10.01.2020

Where is The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act available?

The Act has been notified in the Gazette of India. Act is also available on theofficial website of Ministry (socialjustice.nic.in (https://socialjustice.gov.in/)), National Portal of Transgender Persons (transgender.dosje.gov.in (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/Applicant/Registration/Downloads))

What is the name of Rules framed under the Act?

The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020

When did The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 come into force?

On 29.09.2020

Where are The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 rules available?

The Rules have been notified in the Gazette of India. Rules are also available on the official website of Ministry (socialjustice.nic.in (https://socialjustice.gov.in/)), National Portal of Transgender Persons (transgender.dosje.gov.in (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/Applicant/Registration/Downloads))

What is the name of National Portal?

National Portal for Transgender Persons

When was Portal launched?

On 25.11.2020

What is the web-address of Portal?

https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/ (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/)

What are the details of National Portal for Transgender Person?

The National Portal for Transgender Person assists in applying for a Certificate and Identity card digitally from anywhere in the country. The most important benefit is that it helps the transgender person to get the Certificate of Identity without any physical interface and without having to visit any office. Through the Portal, they can monitor the status of their application that ensures transparency in the process.

Who can apply for Certificate of Identity and Identity Card?

Transgender persons are eligible to apply for certification on the National Portal for Transgender Person.

“transgender person” means a person whose gender does not matchwith the gender assigned to that person at birth and includes trans-manor trans-woman (whether or not such person has undergone SexReassignment Surgery or hormone therapy or laser therapy or suchother therapy), person with intersex variations, gender queer andperson having such socio-cultural identities as kinner, hijra, aravani andjogta.

While applying on the portal for certificate, should the applicantspecify their gender in terms of trans-men or trans-women?

No, the applicant does not have to mention their preferences in terms of trans-men or trans-women, it will be displayed as Transgender person.

Where can the applicant register/apply for the certificate?

Click on this hyperlink: Applicant Registration (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/Applicant/Registration/Index). It will lead the applicant to the home page with sign in/register here option fornew registrants. The applicant after registration can login through thesame page for further process.

What are the basic requirements which have to be fulfilled to acquire the certification?

The following documents are required for becoming eligible for the certification:

  • Proof of residential address (Any) Refer: Form – 1 [See rules 2(d), 3(1)and 6(1)] Transgender Persons (Protection of Right) Rules, 2020 (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/docs/TG%20RULES,%202020.pdf)
  • Photo identification
  • Signature and/or thumb impression
  • Affidavit format and/or medical certificate. Refer: Form – 2 [See rules2(b) and 4(1)] Affidavit Form (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/docs/Affidavit.pdf)
If the applicant is unable to produce residential proof, is there an alternative?

The Applicant may produce an affidavit declaration instead of a residential proof for their certification in case the residential proof is not available.

How to fill the application form?

Manuals in text and video form have been provided on the Portal for the applicants to guide through the procedure of registration. A hyperlink has been provided of the manual for easy access: Manual (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/docs/Manual.pdf). For any technicalquery, kindly contact on the phone number: +91-7923268279.

Is it mandatory for the applicant to apply from their home state(state where they were born) or can they apply for the certification from any other states (presently residing)?

It is not mandatory for the applicant to apply from their home state. However, the Applicant must reside for at least 12 months/ 1 year in other state before applying for the certification.

Is the format for affidavit available on the portal?

Yes, the Affidavit format (English version) is available on the “Download” tab of the home page of National Portal for Transgender person. A hyperlink is provided of the Affidavit format for easy access: Affidavit Form (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/docs/Affidavit.pdf)

What to do if an applicant is unable to fill the form by themselves?

The applicant may visit the nearest office of the Social WelfareDepartment for further information and assistance for filling theapplication form.

Does the applicant have to pay fee for registration form?

No. The application process is free of cost.

How much time will it take for the certification process?

The time taken for processing the application depends on theverification process followed by district up to a maximum of 30 Days.

Is there any helpdesk for the application procedure?

There are two help desks available for assistance.

Administrative query14427mahimanisd@gmail.com (mailto: mahimanisd@gmail.com)
Technical query91-7923268279tghelp@mail.inflibnet.ac.in (mailto: tghelp@mail.inflibnet.ac.in)
Are there any awareness programmes which will be conducted inthe near future?

Online/offline workshops shall be conducted in the future based on requirement. Recent updates on seminars/workshops can be found on the social media handles and website of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowement (http://socialjustice.nic.in (http://socialjustice.nic.in)), National Portal for Transgender persons (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in)) and National Institute of Social Defence (http://www.nisd.gov.in
(http://www.nisd.gov.in))

Is the National Portal for Transgender persons multilingual?

The portal is under process to accommodate multiple languages for a better user experience while filling the application. Currently Portal is available in English, Hindi, Malayalam, Gujarati and Bengali languages.

How much time will it take to receive the certificate of Identity?

The certification takes a maximum of 30 days to process. The Applicant can raise a query on the grievance tab through their registered ID on the portal for follow-up.

When is a medical certificate required?

If a transgender person undergoes medical intervention towards a gender affirming procedure, either as a male or female, such person may apply in the Form – 1, along with a certificate issued to that effect by the Medical Superintendent or Chief Medical Officer of the medical institution in which that person has undergone the said medical intervention, to the District Magistrate for the issue of a revised certificate of identity.

Who will issue the Certificate of Identity and Identity Card?

District Collectors/Magistrate

Do I have to visit District Collectors/Magistrate’s office?

No, process is completely online.

How will I receive the certificate?

Once the Certificate of Identity and Identity card are issued, the applicant can download and print it from the Portal itself.

Do I need to apply separately for Certificate of Identity and Identity Card?

No, on single application for Certificate of Identity and Identity Card would also be issued

What are the benefits of acquiring a Certification/ Transgender person identity card?

The benefits of having a certification/ transgender person identity card are as follows:

  • It helps in identification of the Transgender Person
  • By issuance of these documents, a transgender person is entitled to change name & gender in all official documents.
  • For availing benefits under the Central government schemes and programmes
Which documents are required to apply for a TG Certificate and ID card under section 5 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019?

An Affidavit in the format as given under Form-2 of the said Act along with the filled application.

Is proof of residency mandatory?

For determination of the place of residence, the applicant shall have to reside in the area under the jurisdiction of the District Magistrate as on the date of application and an affidavit to this effect shall be submitted in Form-2.

Is the Psychological Report of the applicant mandatory?

No

Is there any format for a Medical Certificate for a revised Certificate?

There is no specific format for a medical certificate which has to be obtained from the hospital after the gender affirmation surgery. As per the rules it is stated that the district authorities may verify if required but it is not mandatory. Doctor’s notes in the case of international applicants can also be considered.

Having a TG Certificate is necessary while applying for the revisedcertificate under Section 7 of TG Rules 2020?

Having a TG certificate is not mandatory to issue the revised certificate under Section 7 of TG Rules 2020.

Is physical verification to confirm the identity of the applicant as atransgender person from the neighbourhood necessary?

Physical verification to confirm the identity of the applicant as transgender person from the neighbourhood is not necessary, it is a violation of the TG Act, 2019 and should not be practised to issue the certificate & and identity card.

What is a Medical Institution?

As per Section 1 (h) of the said Act, “medical institution” means any medical institution whether hospital or clinic, private or public, in rural areas or urban or overseas.

What is medical intervention?

As per Section 1(i) of the said Act, “medical intervention” includes any gender-affirming medical intervention undertaken by an individual to facilitate the transition to their self-identified gender, including but not limited to counselling, hormonal therapy, and surgical intervention, if any.

What is the remote Area?

Remote areas means tribal areas, villages and other places where no internet or computer facilities are available.

What are the disadvantage conditions?

Disadvantaged conditions include illiterate TG person, mentally ill, handicapped, distressed and other TG persons deem fit.

Who is a minor or a Child?

A person below the age of 18 years is considered a Child as prescribed under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

What is Garima Greh Project?

The Shelter homes for Transgender Persons to be supported by ministry arenamed as Garima Greh.

How many Garima Greh are available at moment in the country?

The ministry has initiated 12 pilot shelter homes namely “Garima Greh” for Transgender Persons. The MoSJ&E provides financial assistance to Community based Organizations (CBOs) for setting up & maintenance of the shelter homes for Transgender Persons.

Where are these Garima Greh?

Garima Greh are in the states of Maharashtra, Delhi, West Bengal, Rajasthan,Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu and Odisha.

What is the objective of Garima Greh?

Main aim of Garima Greh is to provide safe and secure shelter to Transgender persons in need.

What activities are being conducted in Garima Greh?

Garima Greh provides basic amenities like food, medical care, recreational facilities and also conducts capacity-building/skill development programmes for Transgender Persons.

Is there any Covid Advisory issued by the Ministry?

Yes. Ministry has issue an advisory to Transgender Persons regarding Covid appropriate behavior.

Where is Covid Advisory available?

Covid Advisory issued by the Ministry is available on the National Portal for Transgender Persons (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/ (https://transgender.dosje.gov.in/))

What is the objective of this helpline?

To provide psychological support and mental health care to Transgender Persons during Covid lockdown period. The advice on the helpline is provided by professional Psychologists.

sections.heading: Drug Abuse Prevention
sections.html:
Training & Capacity Building:

The Institute runs a number of programmes and training courses, tailored for specific target groups by adopting three-pronged approaches:

  1. Three Month Certificate Course on Drug De-Addiction, Counselling Skills, Treatment & Rehabilitation: The course has been designed to build the knowledge base of service providers including Counsellors, Social Workers, Outreach Workers of treatment centers. The course includes interactive theoretical sessions and Field Placement for a period of One Month at NDDTC, AIIMS and other De-Addiction Centre in Delhi. The broad contents of the course are – Basics of Addiction, Motivation and Counselling, Community Based interventions, Outreach and Awareness Creation.
  2. Fifteen-Day Certificate Course on Drug Abuse Prevention by the National Institute of Social Defence and State level Coordinating Agencies (SLCAs).
  3. Five-Day Training Course on Drug Abuse Prevention by the National Institute of Social Defence and State level Coordinating Agencies (SLCAs).
Thematic Skill Building Programmes:

Under this category, the following two to five days’ programmes are undertaken:

  • Substance Addiction Identification, Initial Motivation and Early Intervention: To orient service providers on symptomatic behaviour, early identification and early warning signs in order to equip them with requisite techniques for early intervention.
  • Counselling for Addiction (Individual, Family and Group): To train counsellors working in the areas of substance demand reduction so as to expand their knowledge base and sharpen their individual, group and family counselling skills.
  • Preventive Interventions for High-Risk Groups: To sensitise service providers working with high-risk groups such as truckers, commercial sex-workers, etc., on issues pertaining to Behavioural Change Communication (BCC).
  • Research, Rapid Assessment & Monitoring of Substance Abuse: On the relevance, scope and contents of research, rapid assessment and monitoring of substance abuse to obtain evidence for planning strategic interventions.
  • Management of Co-dependency and Family Issues: To enable Counsellors/ Social Workers to deal effectively with significant others including family and co-dependents of addicts.
  • Rehabilitation and Relapse Prevention – Issues & Modalities: For service providers for development and implementation of rehabilitation and relapse prevention programmes.
  • Prevention and Management of Substance Abuse and HIV/AIDS: To orient and expose the service providers to the area of HIV/AIDS prevention among substance users.
  • Alcohol and Substance Abuse Prevention at Workplace: To sensitize Labour Welfare Officers of Corporate houses and Project Officers/Senior Counsellors of Treatment-cum-Rehabilitation Centres working with the organizations/ enterprises/industries.
  • A Learning Pack for Youth Coordinators: Designed for youth coordinators of National Service Scheme (NSS) and Nehru Yuva Kendra (NYK) on alcohol and substance abuse prevention.
  • Treatment and Rehabilitation of Substance Addicts in Prisons/ Correctional Settings: To sensitize and empower middle level functionaries working in prisons/correctional settings on alcohol and substance abuse prevention issues.
  • Documentation for Addiction Management-Assessment, Client Profiling, Recording and Documentation: To ensure proper recording and documentation of programme activities.
  • Management Development Programme (MDP): To provide basic skills and understanding of the programme activities being carried out by Treatment-cum-Rehabilitation Centres.
  • Orientation Course based on TNA (Training Needs Assessment): On the selected thematic issues relating to treatment based on needs assessment in operational areas of SLCAs.

Strategic Consultations
The Institute also organises strategic consultations with various stakeholders to evolve strategies for convergent action so as to bring synergy in ongoing programmes with different partners.
The Institute also holds Annual Consultative Meets with the State level Coordinating Agencies (SLCAs) located in different parts of the country which serve as regional extension centres. This consultative meet is organised every year to plan out the activities of NCDAP and SLCAs for strategizing key interventions based on emerging trends, evidence and experience gained at the operational level.

Old Age Care

Training & Capacity Building:
The long-term, short-term and thematic-based courses that are presently being carried out by NISD/collaborating organisations are:

1. PG Diploma in Integrated Geriatric Care
Target Group: An individual having graduation and above educational qualification and interested in working in this field.

Aims and Objectives:

  • Develop a cadre of frontline skilled/trained personnel of geriatric care
  • Provide a comprehensive and scientific knowledge base on various aspects relating to the geriatric care
  • Develop an appropriate aptitude and skill for working with older persons

The course curriculum broadly includes:

  • Gerontology
  • Public Policy and Planning
  • Clinical Geriatrics
  • Geriatric Management
  • Psychology and Counselling
  • Research Methodology

Academic inputs include:

  1. Seminar Presentation
  2. Dissertation
  3. Group Project
  4. Field work/Placement

Duration of the Course: 1 Year
Number of Seats: 25
Announcement of the Course in National/Regional Dailies: May/June

Admission to the course is made on the basis of Common Aptitude Test (CAT) held on all-India basis, group discussion and interview.

Tentative Date of Commencement of Course: October 1

Career Prospects:
The career opportunities for the post-graduate course could range from non-governmental sectors, government sectors, corporate sectors and academic institutions as:

  • Project Director/Programme Managers
  • Counsellors & Consultants in CBO
  • Associates with RWA and NGOs
  • Professionals in Hospital Settings
  • Prospective Faculty Members and Instructors/Trainers in Academic Institutes

2. Certificate Courses in Geriatric Care
(i) Three-Month Basic Course for Caregivers /Bed Assistants

Target Group: Any individual having passed 10th standard, having a desire to serve senior citizens.

Aims & Objectives:

  • Create a cadre of caregivers in bed-care assistance, etc
  • Provide palliative care services, emergency and crisis-management

Course Curriculum includes:

  • Introduction to NISD
  • Body system, functions & related problems in Elderly
  • Mental Health Issues Concerns in Elderly
  • Communication
  • Infection Prevention & Control
  • Nutrition
  • Positions, Use of comfort devices and Assistive Devices

Practical training inputs include:

sections.heading: Drug Abuse Monitoring System (DAMS)
sections.html:
Drug Abuse Monitoring System (DAMS) is an online database, wherein data on the types of substances, method of consumption, clinical and general profile of treatment seekers at de-addiction centres will be collected on a quarterly basis for understanding the trends of the substance abuse in the country. This system is to further strengthen the existing interventions and would be useful for developing appropriate preventive strategies in changing substance consumption behaviours.

Outreach/ Promotional Activities through the Regional Resource and Training Centres (RRTCs)
The Eleven Numbers of NGOs and One State Govt. Social Welfare Board have been designated as RRTCs to provide training to the service providers of the ministry-supported (IRCAs), Drug Treatment and Counseling Centres, for enhancing their capacity, at regional levels. This is considered desirable and pragmatic in view of the size of the country and regional variations necessitating specific strategies.
Besides, RRTCs also provide the following services to the NGOs working in the field of Substance Abuse Prevention:
• Documentation of all activities of the NGOs, including preparation of Information Education Communication (IEC) Material.
• Undertaking advocacy, research and monitoring of substance abuse programmes
• Technical support to the NGOs, community-based organisation and enterprises.

Observance of “The International Day Against Substance Abuse and Illicit Trafficking”
On 26 June every year, NISD in collaboration with the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment observes “The International Day Against Substance Abuse and Illicit Trafficking” to sensitise the society, particularly the youth, about the menace of substance abuse.
A manual on the minimum standards of services for the programmes under the scheme for the prevention of alcoholism & substance (substances) abuse have been developed for IRCAs/treatment centres run by NGOs funded by the Ministry.
A manual on the implementation framework of the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction to focus on preventive education, awareness generation, identification, counseling, treatment and rehabilitation of drug dependent persons and training and capacity building of the service providers through collaborative efforts of the central and state governments and NGOs.
